purpose: Define the atomicity, error-surfacing, and downstream-exit-code effect of every file write a caliper-docgen CLI subcommand performs, so a failed or interrupted write via extract --out or watch --out can never leave a truncated file at the target path, and so a write failure is always surfaced rather than silently swallowed.
scope: crates/cli/src/output.rs (the shared write_atomic helper) and its two call sites: crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs's --out handling and crates/cli/src/commands/watch.rs's --out handling. Covers: which commands write files at all, the temp-file-then-rename mechanism's success/failure behavior, and how each caller (extract vs. watch) surfaces a write failure — extract propagates as a hard Err, watch degrades to a Diagnostic and keeps running.
non_goals: The extraction/resolution logic itself — owned by crates/core, a separate capability under a separate spec.
NAPI/Node binding entry points — owned by crates/binding, a separate capability.

The general exit-code contract for extract/watch/check/inspect on extraction diagnostics (Error/Warning severity, --strict) — covered by SPEC-CLI-001a. This spec covers only the exit-code effect of a *write failure* specifically.

LSP framing/allocation and config-loading semantics — covered by SPEC-CLI-001c and SPEC-CLI-001d respectively; neither lsp nor schema/completions writes to a file path (AC-001), so this spec has no criteria for them beyond that enumeration.
The RDT/Storybook serializer output shape and the composes field round-trip — already covered by extract.rs's own existing tests, not part of this contract.

Extracting watch.rs's inline --out write branch (inside the Watchexec::new action closure) into a directly-callable, unit-testable function mirroring watch_exit_code's existing seam. AC-005/AC-006/AC-007 are grounded directly in source and verified by live manual runs rather than an automated unit test in this revision; that refactor is a testability improvement, not a correctness gap, and is out of scope here.

Surfacing a snapshot-serialization failure in watch --out as a Diagnostic. watch.rs's --out branch opens with `if let Ok(json) = serde_json::to_string(&snapshot)`; on Err (which ExtractionOutput's current field types cannot actually produce, since none of its fields include non-finite floats, non-UTF-8 strings, or non-string map keys — the only conditions serde_json::to_string can fail on), the write is silently skipped with no Diagnostic and no exit-code effect, leaving PATH with stale contents from a prior successful write. This is a real, unaddressed violation of CLAUDE.md's 'always emit a Diagnostic when degrading' rule, but is not reachable by any acceptance criterion in this spec since ExtractionOutput cannot currently serialize to Err — fixing it (adding a Diagnostic on this branch) is a follow-up hardening change, not something this spec's criteria can exercise.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: extract and watch are the only two commands whose own CLI-layer code (crates/cli/src/commands/*.rs) writes to a user-specified path. check, inspect, schema, lsp, and completions contain no call to any file-writing API (write_atomic, std::fs::write, std::fs::File::create, std::fs::OpenOptions, std::fs::copy, std::fs::rename, or any tokio::fs equivalent) outside #[cfg(test)] modules anywhere in crates/cli/src/commands/{check,inspect,schema,lsp,completions}.rs. (Scope note: crates/core's DtsCache may separately persist a .d.ts parse cache to a cache_dir on behalf of any command including check/inspect, via pipeline::extract — that cache persistence is crates/core's own concern, not this CLI-layer contract, and is out of scope here.)

When extract --out PATH is passed without --json and the write succeeds, the bytes at PATH after the write are byte-identical to what the same invocation with --out omitted would print to stdout (the same --format-dependent serialization — canonical/RDT/storybook JSON or TOON — that extract.rs's stdout arm produces via println!), with that stdout arm's single trailing newline removed, and with every occurrence of a run-to-run-variable stats value — the "durationMs" JSON key and the "dtsCacheHits" JSON key for canonical/rdt/storybook, or the durationMs= and cacheHits= values on TOON's stats: line — replaced by a fixed placeholder in both the PATH bytes and the stdout bytes before comparing them, since both values can legitimately differ between the two separate process runs being compared (duration is wall-clock-dependent; dtsCacheHits/cacheHits differs whenever the second run's read of a .d.ts file hits a cache the first run itself populated). No file named by prepending a dot to PATH's full file name (including its extension) and appending '.tmp' remains in PATH's parent directory afterward — e.g. for PATH ending in out.json, no .out.json.tmp file remains (write_atomic's same-directory-temp-then-rename mechanism).

When extract --out PATH is passed without --json and the write fails for any reason (missing parent directory, permission denied, disk full, or any other io::Error from write_atomic other than a rename-step failure covered by AC-004), the process exits with code 1, stderr contains an error whose text includes both 'Writing to {PATH}' and the underlying io::Error's message, PATH is left untouched (no partial file created at PATH), and the same-directory temp file created during the write is removed rather than left behind. (Implementation note, not part of the pass/fail check: achieved by .wrap_err(...) and ? propagation out of cmd_extract and then out of main().)

When extract --out PATH is passed without --json and the write fails at the rename step (e.g. PATH already exists as a directory), the same-directory temp file created during the write is removed rather than left behind, and the failure is surfaced to stderr via the same exit-code-1 path as AC-003.

When watch --out PATH successfully writes a snapshot, PATH parses as valid, compact (no pretty-printing) single-line JSON with no trailing newline, and whose top-level 'components' key's set of object keys equals the set of component keys that a one-shot extract of the same watched source directories at that point in time would produce — where a component key is its bare display name unless that display name collides with another component's in the same tree, in which case both are keyed as "{displayName} ({filePath})" instead — and whose 'stats.componentsExtracted' field equals the size of that same key set. No file named by prepending a dot to PATH's full file name (including its extension) and appending '.tmp' remains in PATH's parent directory afterward. (Verification note, not part of the pass/fail check: the --out write is a branch inside watch.rs's Watchexec::new action closure with no standalone unit-testable seam today, so confirming this requires running watch --out PATH, triggering a file-change event, and inspecting PATH and its directory afterward, rather than a unit test.)

When watch --out PATH's write fails for any reason (missing parent directory, permission denied, disk full, or any other io::Error from write_atomic), a single Error-severity Diagnostic (DiagnosticCode::IoError) naming PATH is printed to stderr, the value stored into watch's tracked exit-code atomic by watch_exit_code(&snapshot) — which runs before the --out write is attempted — is neither read nor modified by the write-failure path, so the process's eventual exit code is identical to what the same run would produce had the write succeeded, and the watch session continues processing subsequent file-change events rather than terminating. (Implementation note, not part of the pass/fail check: this is achieved by catching the Err inside cmd_watch's watchexec closure and converting it to a Diagnostic rather than propagating it as a Rust-level Err. Verification note: same as AC-005 — no standalone unit-testable seam exists today; confirming this requires a live watch --out PATH session with an unwritable PATH.)

When watch --out PATH's write fails specifically at the rename step, the same-directory temp file created during the write is removed rather than left behind, in addition to the Diagnostic surfacing described in AC-006.

When extract --json --out PATH is passed together, --out is ignored entirely — no write_atomic call occurs, PATH is not created or modified, and no Diagnostic or error is emitted regarding the ignored --out flag; stdout receives the compact canonical JSON exactly as extract --json alone would produce.
